summary: Benin’s pledges combine restoration, conservation and agricultural transformation. For restoration, it targets at least 15,000 ha of reforestation annually through 2035 (150,000 ha), with a later target of 30,000 ha/year from 2029, equivalent to 210,000 ha by 2035; the latter cumulative area is about 4.5% of the country’s 47,057 km² forest cover. Conservation measures include cutting net deforestation to no more than 35,000 ha/year by 2035 and placing 950,958 ha under sustainable forest management in 2026–2030, with separate targets of 300,000 ha in 2028–2030 and 506,280 ha in 2030–2035. Agriculture dominates by scale: improved techniques and soil-fertility maintenance each cover 5,000,000 ha in 2021–2030, equivalent to about 117% of current agricultural area, while water-controlled rice land rises to 52,000 ha by 2035 and 70,000 ha by 2040. Integrated projects include 140,000 ha of mangrove restoration and 100,000 ha of old-cashew-plantation rehabilitation.
